title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless spec is now 3 days out — the breaking rewrite ratifies Tuesday
bullets.summary: The largest revision of the protocol since launch (stateless core with no session id, any request to any instance, OAuth-aligned auth, a formal deprecation policy) plus MCP Apps (server-rendered UI) and the Tasks extension ratify Jul 28; beta SDKs are already shipping.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is 3 days from a breaking change; the migration inventory + hardening checklist has to close before Tuesday, and the Tasks extension maps straight onto our long-running scan jobs. Load-bearing action of the week.

bullets.title: Guideline launches an Ad Intelligence MCP Server — proprietary ad-spend/pricing data now agent-callable (Jul 22)
bullets.summary: Guideline exposes its global ad spend, pricing, and market-intelligence data through a standards-based MCP layer callable from Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, or a client's own agents.
bullets.how: Feeds Brand 9 Signs paid-media planning and PRAGMA's operator wedge with real competitive spend/pricing signal; a Construct media-ops agent can pull benchmark rates before it sets a bid.

bullets.title: xAI ships Grok STT 1.0 — a dedicated speech-to-text model (Jul 23, on LLM Gateway Jul 24)
bullets.summary: xAI adds a standalone speech-to-text model to the Grok line, now routable through LLM Gateway alongside the frontier chat models.
bullets.how: A cheap, swappable transcription front-end for dictated triage and voice capture into Construct agents (Bobby's mobile workflow); evaluate against our current STT before wiring anything load-bearing to it.

bullets.title: Axonius launches an AI Agent + MCP Server for asset intelligence (Jul 21)
bullets.summary: Axonius connects its asset-inventory and security-posture data to enterprise AI through an agent + MCP server, so an agent can query what's deployed and where the exposures are.
bullets.how: The pattern, not the product, is the lesson: an asset/tool inventory + posture check is exactly what The Construct's own MCP fleet needs as the Jul-28 migration lands; treat our connectors as governed assets with least-authority scoping.

bullets.title: Pixazo ships MCP servers for Nano Banana, Seedance, Runway, and Flux — top image/video models now native inside MCP clients (Jul 16)
bullets.summary: Pixazo exposes best-in-class image and video generation models as dedicated MCP servers, giving an agent direct access to each model without a bespoke integration.
bullets.how: Complements the Revid.ai end-to-end pipeline already on the board: this is the model-access layer, so one Construct creative agent can pick the right image/video model per Brand 9 Signs signage brief and render in-flow.

praxis_lesson: With Opus 5 shipped (Jul 24) and now the fleet default, the "which model" question is settled for the quarter — the live risk has moved to the plumbing. The Jul-28 stateless-MCP rewrite is 3 days out and every write-capable connector we run touches it, so this week's discipline is inventory-and-harden (Axonius's own pitch is the tell): treat each MCP server as a governed asset with least-authority scoping and a migration checklist, not a loose integration. The new data/creative MCPs (Guideline, Pixazo) are worth wiring only after the fleet clears the migration clean.
